typeName: Table of f, g and their derivatives
title: Two functions from a table: product, quotient, tangent line and a limit

stimulus.title: Values of f, g and their derivatives
stimulus.html:
The functions ff and gg are differentiable for all real numbers. The table gives values of the functions and their derivatives at selected values of xx. No calculator is allowed.

Values of f(x)f(x), f′(x)f'(x), g(x)g(x) and g′(x)g'(x)
xx1234
f(x)f(x)4136
f′(x)f'(x)−2-2351
g(x)g(x)132−1-1
g′(x)g'(x)4−2-23−4-4

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Let h(x)=f(x)g(x)h(x) = f(x)g(x). Find h′(2)h'(2). Show the work that leads to your answer.

rubric.point: Product rule with the table values: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h'(2) = f'(2)g(2) + f(2)g'(2)</annotation></semantics></math>. Not earned by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(2)g'(2)</annotation></semantics></math>, the product of the derivatives.
accept: the two terms in either order, with table values substituted

rubric.point: Answer: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h'(2) = 7</annotation></semantics></math>, with the product-rule setup

parts.sample: By the product rule, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h'(x) = f'(x)g(x) + f(x)g'(x)</annotation></semantics></math>. So <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h'(2) = f'(2)g(2) + f(2)g'(2) = (3)(3) + (1)(-2) = 9 - 2 = 7</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Let k(x)=f(x)g(x)k(x) = \frac{f(x)}{g(x)}. Find k′(3)k'(3). Show the work that leads to your answer.

rubric.point: Quotient rule with the table values: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k'(3) = \frac{f'(3)g(3) - f(3)g'(3)}{\left( g(3) \right)^2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Not earned with the numerator reversed or the denominator not squared.

Answer: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k'(3) = \frac{1}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>, with the quotient-rule setup

parts.sample: By the quotient rule, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k'(x) = \frac{f'(x)g(x) - f(x)g'(x)}{\left( g(x) \right)^2}</annotation></semantics></math>. So <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k'(3) = \frac{(5)(2) - (3)(3)}{(2)^2} = \frac{10 - 9}{4} = \frac{1}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Let m(x)=4f(x)−ln⁡xm(x) = 4f(x) - \ln x for x>0x > 0. Write an equation for the line tangent to the graph of mm at x=1x = 1.

rubric.point: Slope: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>1</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m'(1) = 4f'(1) - \frac{1}{1} = -9</annotation></semantics></math>

Tangent line through <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>16</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, m(1)) = (1, 16)</annotation></semantics></math> with the slope found: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 16 - 9(x - 1)</annotation></semantics></math>. The height needs <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m(1) = 4(4) - \ln 1 = 16</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m(1) = 4f(1) - \ln 1 = 4(4) - 0 = 16</annotation></semantics></math>. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m'(x) = 4f'(x) - \frac{1}{x}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m'(1) = 4(-2) - 1 = -9</annotation></semantics></math>. The tangent line is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 16 - 9(x - 1)</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt:
(i) Find limx→4f(x)−6x−4\lim_{x \to 4} \frac{f(x) - 6}{x - 4}. Explain your reasoning.
(ii) Explain why there must be a value cc, with 1<c<41 < c < 4, such that g(c)=0g(c) = 0.

rubric.point: (i) The limit is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(4) = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(4) = 6</annotation></semantics></math> makes it the definition of the derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 4</annotation></semantics></math>. The bare answer 1, with no link to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(4)</annotation></semantics></math>, does not earn the point; neither does writing <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>0</mn><mn>0</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{0}{0} = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

(ii) Continuity with its reason: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> is differentiable, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 4]</annotation></semantics></math>. Not earned by "<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous" with no reason.
accept: g is differentiable, therefore continuous on the interval

rubric.point: (ii) Conclusion, with the continuity point: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn><mo>></mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(1) = 1 > 0 > -1 = g(4)</annotation></semantics></math>, so by the Intermediate Value Theorem there is a <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, 4)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(c) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample:
(i) Since f(4)=6f(4) = 6, f(x)−6x−4=f(x)−f(4)x−4\frac{f(x) - 6}{x - 4} = \frac{f(x) - f(4)}{x - 4}, so the limit is the definition of f′(4)f'(4). From the table, limx→4f(x)−6x−4=f′(4)=1\lim_{x \to 4} \frac{f(x) - 6}{x - 4} = f'(4) = 1.
(ii) gg is differentiable, so gg is continuous on [1,4][1, 4]. Also g(1)=1g(1) = 1 and g(4)=−1g(4) = -1, so 0 is between g(4)g(4) and g(1)g(1). By the Intermediate Value Theorem, there is a value cc with 1<c<41 < c < 4 such that g(c)=0g(c) = 0.
